      <description><p>The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?</p><p>Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.</p><p>It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/26/lana-nusseibeh-uae-sudan-un-secretary-general">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/25/people-killed-fuel-tanker-crash-ignites-large-fire-cairo-highway</link>
      <description><p>Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred</p><p>A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.</p><p>The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/25/people-killed-fuel-tanker-crash-ignites-large-fire-cairo-highway">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/25/swiss-tourist-killed-british-americans-injured-elephants-cameroon</link>
      <description><p>Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park</p><p>A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.</p><p>The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/25/swiss-tourist-killed-british-americans-injured-elephants-cameroon">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa</p><p>When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard.       <description><p>Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages</p><p>Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.</p><p>Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/24/cartagena-colombia-hostages-supermarket">Continue reading...</a></description>
